name: Asmalı Meyhane
address: Çınar Çarşı Caddesi No. 20, Cumhuriyet Mah., 17680 Bozcaada
tier: THE BERTHS · THE MEYHANE TABLES — SQUID ON THE COALS, MEZE IN WAVES
recognition: Opened in 1950 by Niko Manalodis and his brothers (Daily Sabah)
what_to_order: Grilled island kalamar|Raw fish with basil|Cevizli ahtapot|Rezeneli sübye|Kabak çiçeği dolması|Karides cızlama
reservation: Book in summer; call ahead off-season to check it is serving
notes: Grilled island kalamar, then raw fish with basil.
verdict: Order the grilled kalamar and the raw fish and let the counter choose the rest; that is where the kitchen is strongest. Online reviews are mixed, with praise for the meze and the staff and complaints about price and slow service at busy times. Go early in the evening, before the summer crowd fills the stairs.
caveat: No 2026-dated evidence and no winter dates found; reviews mention high prices and uneven service on busy nights.

name: Sandal Restaurant
neighborhood: Alsancak Sokak, the old bazaar street
address: Alsancak Sokak No. 31, Cumhuriyet Mah., 17680 Bozcaada
tier: THE MEYHANE TABLES — SQUID ON THE COALS, MEZE IN WAVES
recognition: Called an island classic by Yemek.com; building was Apostol Kalfa's coffeehouse (Onedio)
what_to_order: Sandal borani|Ada otları salatası|Damla sakızlı enginar|Ahtapot salata|Midye dolma|Grilled kalamar
reservation: Reserve well ahead for dinner in season (Yemek.com)
notes: Sandal borani and the island herb salad, then grilled squid.
verdict: Yemek.com calls it an island classic, and every guide we found sends you here for the meze and the squid rather than for a view. It is a lane, not a harbour terrace. Evenings are hard to get even in September and October, so book days ahead in season and call to confirm it is open out of season.
caveat: Book days ahead for dinner in season; no 2026-dated evidence or winter dates found.

name: Nevreste
address: Alsancak Sokak No. 22, Cumhuriyet Mah., 17680 Bozcaada
tier: THE MEYHANE TABLES — SQUID ON THE COALS, MEZE IN WAVES
recognition: Dinner under the yediveren rose tree; signature Bozcaada Bombası
reservation: Book ahead for dinner in summer and on holidays
notes: The Bozcaada Bombası, then grilled sea bass.
verdict: On review volume and score it is the most-praised table on the island right now (Restaurant Guru 4.9 from about 4,660 votes; Foursquare is cooler at 7.7). Treat it as the long dinner, not a quick stop: meze first, then fish. Book a day or two ahead in summer. We found nothing dated 2026 and no winter dates, so call before you go.
caveat: Book ahead for summer and holiday dinners; no winter or 2026 dates found, call first.

name: Dört Hanımeli
tier: EV YEMEĞI — THE ISLAND'S HOME COOKING
recognition: Founded more than forty years ago by retired primary-school teachers
verdict: Come for lunch and the mantı; it is the reason to cross town, and the olive-oil vegetables are the reason to stay. Do not expect a sea view or a fish grill. The evidence is reviews without dates, so treat the details as likely rather than certain, and check it is open before planning around it.
caveat: Home cooking with no sea view; no 2026-dated evidence or winter dates found, call ahead.

name: Ada'm
address: Alsancak Sokak No. 42, Cumhuriyet Mah., 17680 Bozcaada
tier: EV YEMEĞI — THE ISLAND'S HOME COOKING
recognition: Yemek.com: 'now an island classic'; about ten years trading (Oggusto)
what_to_order: Enginarlı ahtapot|Asma yaprağında levrek|Deniz mahsullü midye
reservation: Book in high season; call ahead off-season
notes: Enginarlı ahtapot: octopus with artichokes in cream.
verdict: The cheaper, looser alternative to the set-piece meze houses, and the place for a cook's own dishes rather than the island canon. Order the octopus with artichokes. Reviews on the room are mixed, so come for the plates. Nothing found is dated 2026 and no winter dates exist online, so call before you go.
caveat: Small, plain room with mixed reviews on comfort; no 2026-dated evidence or winter dates found.

name: Talay Şarapçılık
address: Shop in town: Lale Sok. 5, Bozcaada (Frommer's); Wanderlog lists it as 'Talay Şarap Satış Mağazası Meydan'
tier: THE BERTHS · AT THE CELLAR DOOR — THE ISLAND'S OWN GRAPES
recognition: Founded 1948 by the Talay brothers; bottled wine from 1955 (Le Petit Journal Istanbul)
notes: A paid flight at the town shop, ending on the Cabernet Sauvignon-Kuntra red
verdict: The plainest way to taste Bozcaada's own grapes without a car or a booking: a working family producer, not a showpiece estate. Expect a shop counter rather than a cellar tour, and modest prices against the boutique labels. Whether the counter keeps winter hours is not published anywhere we could find, so treat a November visit as a phone call first.
caveat: A sales shop, not a cellar tour; no published winter hours found, call before going in November-April
hot_this_month: The island's oldest family winery pours its own Vasilaki and Karalahna at the town counter; November hours not posted, so call first.

name: Corvus Vineyards
neighborhood: Among the vines at Tuzburnu, outside town
tier: AT THE CELLAR DOOR — THE ISLAND'S OWN GRAPES
recognition: JancisRobinson.com carries tasting notes for Corvus Corpus 2004, 2005 and 2006; the 17/20 score for 2004 could not be read in search
what_to_order: Corpus|Çavuş white|Zeleia Vasilaki|Blend Bianco|Cru Turk red
reservation: Contact the winery before going; visiting days are limited
notes: A glass of the Çavuş white, then the Corpus red, at the Wine and Bite on the estate
verdict: The island's most internationally reviewed label and the bottle to open if a guest wants proof that Bozcaada can make a serious wine. It is also the dearest: one visitor found the island shop dearer than Ankara retail. Visiting has long been seasonal (a 2009 guide gave June to September for cellar tastings), and we found no current winter schedule, so do not plan an off-season visit without a reply from the winery.
caveat: Estate outside town; tastings historically summer-only (June-September in 2009); no 2026 winter hours found; island prices can exceed city retail
hot_this_month: Ask what the 2026 Çavuş, picked in August, is doing in tank; visiting days are limited, so check before you drive out.

name: Amadeus MMX
tier: AT THE CELLAR DOOR — THE ISLAND'S OWN GRAPES
recognition: Lonely Planet lists Amadeus Vineyard: 'a convivial and engaging host', the Cabernets 'particularly impressive'
notes: The Cuvée Blanche, then the Grillo with the island's vegetable and fish mezes
verdict: Go for the host and the oddities: grapes you will not taste anywhere else in Turkey, poured by the man who planted them, and bottles that are hard to find even in Istanbul. Lonely Planet rates the Cabernets. It is a small operation outside town with no published visiting hours, and nothing we found says it receives visitors in winter, so message ahead.
caveat: Small family cellar outside town, own transport needed; no published hours or winter opening found; message before going

name: Bozcaada Wednesday Market
tier: THE BERTHS · LA RUE — THE MARKET AND THE PASTANE
recognition: A weekly market with the castle as its backdrop (GoTürkiye/CNN sponsored feature, 2026); Wednesday per Coast Guide Turkey
what_to_order: Domates reçeli|Fig jam|Garlic confit|Local goat cheese and Ezine cheese|Almond-mastic cookies|Island tomatoes and Çavuş grapes
notes: Domates reçeli (tomato jam) with a wedge of local goat cheese
verdict: The one place to buy island produce from the person who grew it, and the best shopping stop for a galley. But the details are soft: most sources say Wednesday, one says Friday, and Katie Parla noted the weekly market had moved without saying where. Ask at the harbour or the municipality which day and square it uses this winter before planning around it.
caveat: Day and site disputed (Wednesday in most sources, Friday in one; Parla reports it moved); winter running not confirmed; bring cash
hot_this_month: The islanders' own weekly market, for those who stay the winter; ask in town where and whether it stands this week, and bring cash.

name: Çiçek Pastanesi Tahir Usta
tier: LA RUE — THE MARKET AND THE PASTANE
recognition: Gazete Vatan: pastries baked in a stone oven over wood fire, from recipes of the island's Rum kitchens
what_to_order: Damla sakızlı bademli kurabiye|Mastic ice cream|Wild-fig ice cream|Lavender ice cream|Island breakfast|Wood-fired hamur işleri
notes: Damla sakızlı bademli kurabiye, plus a scoop of wild-fig or mastic ice cream
verdict: The island's breakfast-and-sweets stop, worth it for the cookie and the fig ice cream, not as a meal. It has not been touched by the chains. The catch is the calendar: one Hürriyet column describes the island shop as the family's summer branch, so in November it may be shut. Check before promising guests an ice cream.
caveat: Counter and breakfast place, not dinner; the island branch may be summer-only (Hürriyet), ice-cream flavours rotate and are seasonal
